A complete flowering dicot plant (e.g., cowpea or tomato). The diagram shows the underground taproot system with primary and lateral roots, and the above-ground shoot system. The shoot shows a main stem with nodes and internodes, leaves with a petiole and network of veins, a flower showing petals and central reproductive parts, and a developing fruit (pod).

A three-panel comparison diagram of Monocots vs Dicots. Panel 1: Seeds - a maize grain (monocot) showing a single cotyledon, next to a split cowpea seed (dicot) showing two cotyledons. Panel 2: Leaves - a long narrow maize leaf with parallel veins (monocot), next to a broad cowpea leaf with a network of branching veins (dicot). Panel 3: Roots - a fibrous root system with many equal-sized roots branching from the stem base (monocot), next to a taproot system showing one thick main root with small side branches (dicot). Clear labels for each.

Comparison diagram showing the external and internal structures of a Yam tuber (Stem tuber) and a Cassava tuber (Root tuber). Left side: Yam tuber showing external "eyes"/buds and fine roots; cut-away showing thin peel and massive starchy core without a woody center. Right side: Cassava tuber showing smooth external surface without buds; cut-away showing outer brown peel, inner thick cortex, white starchy core, and a prominent woody central vascular strand.

Cross-section of an Onion bulb. The diagram shows the bulb cut vertically. At the very bottom is a flat horizontal disc with roots growing down. Above the disc are thick, concentric overlapping layers. At the very center is a small bud pointing upward. The outermost layer is thin and papery.
